title: What Is Claude Cowork? Anthropic's Agent for Knowledge Work Explained

blocks.text: What Is Claude Cowork? Anthropic's Agent for Knowledge Work Explained
Claude Cowork is Anthropic's agentic tool for non-coding knowledge work: connect a folder, describe a goal, and it plans and executes multi-step tasks. What it is, pricing, and availability.

Claude Cowork is Anthropic's agentic tool for knowledge work: you hand it a folder, a goal, and any apps it needs, and it plans a multi-step task, executes it, and hands back a finished file for you to review. It first shipped as a desktop app in January 2026 and went generally available on every paid Claude plan on April 9, 2026. As of July 7, 2026, Anthropic began rolling it out to web and mobile too, in beta, starting with Max subscribers.

Where Claude Code is built for people who write software, Cowork is built for people who don't want a terminal: operators, analysts, chiefs of staff, founders, and anyone who spends their day moving information between documents, spreadsheets, and apps. Anthropic's own sample of 1.2 million Cowork sessions from May 2026 found the largest use case, at 33.4%, was business process and operations work: pulling scattered updates into a report, building onboarding checklists, reconciling spreadsheets. Software development accounted for just 8.7% of sessions, which tracks: that's what Claude Code is for.
How Claude Cowork actually works

You open the Claude Desktop app, switch to Cowork, connect a folder, and describe what you want done. Claude reads that request, breaks it into subtasks, and works through them in an isolated server environment, reading and writing files only in the folders you've explicitly connected. It can open a browser for web-based steps, and it connects to apps like Slack, plus CRM, email, and calendar tools, with additional deployment options through Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry. Anthropic also ships a growing library of pre-built plugins, including Brand Voice, Legal, and Finance, that install without any setup.
A few things distinguish it from just chatting with Claude:
It ships with pre-built skills, connectors, and plugins, including Brand Voice, Legal, and Finance plugins, ready to use without any setup.
It runs unattended. Scheduled tasks (type /schedule in a session) run in the background on Anthropic's servers, so they don't need your laptop open or awake.
It works in parallel. Large projects get split into concurrent subtasks rather than run one step at a time.
You stay in the loop. Cowork gives real-time visibility into each action it takes, and three permission modes (Manual, Auto, Skip) control how much it does before checking with you.

As of July 2026, chat and Cowork share the same home on web and desktop, with projects and files available in both. The desktop app stays the primary place for anything touching your local files or a browser.

Claude Cowork vs Claude Code, in one paragraph

Both products run on the same underlying Claude models and the same agentic architecture: plan, act, check the work. The split is who they're for. Claude Code lives in a terminal, an IDE, or Slack, and gives a developer full control over a coding workflow, at the cost of a real setup: installing the CLI, learning terminal patterns, configuring permissions. Cowork skips all of that. You point it at a folder and describe a goal in plain language, and it handles document-heavy, file-intensive work without you touching a command line. If you're deciding which one your team actually needs, the full Claude Cowork vs Claude Code comparison breaks down the decision by job, not by hype.

Pricing
Cowork is included on every paid Claude plan. There's no separate Cowork subscription and no Cowork-only tier.

Cowork sessions draw down the same usage pool as chat, and Anthropic notes Cowork tasks consume that capacity faster than a normal conversation. (Cowork itself doesn't have a separate price tied to which model answers your requests; if you're also comparing what Anthropic charges for its flagship model directly, see Claude Fable 5 pricing explained.) To mark the mobile and web launch, Anthropic is extending doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5, 2026, though that's a time-limited promotion, not a permanent change.

Availability

Cowork's desktop app runs on macOS, Windows (x64 and arm64), ChromeOS, and Linux, per Anthropic's official product page. Web and mobile access is in beta, rolling out first to Max subscribers with more plans to follow over the following weeks. If you're on Pro or Team and don't see Cowork on web or mobile yet, that's expected: the beta is staged, not a single flip.
FAQ

What is Claude Cowork? Claude Cowork is Anthropic's agentic tool for non-coding knowledge work. You connect a folder or app, describe a task, and Claude plans and executes it end to end, producing a real file (a document, spreadsheet, or deck) rather than just a chat answer.
Is Claude Cowork free? No. Cowork requires a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise). The free tier includes chat only.

Is Claude Cowork the same as Claude Code? No. Both are built on the same Claude models, but Claude Code is for software development in a terminal or IDE, and Cowork is for business, research, and document work through a point-and-click desktop app. See the full comparison.

Can Claude Cowork access my entire computer? No. It can only read and write files in folders you've explicitly connected, and network access follows the egress settings you've configured for that session.
Does Claude Cowork work on mobile? Yes, in beta as of July 7, 2026. Access is rolling out first to Max subscribers, with Pro and Team plans following in the weeks after.

What can I actually use Claude Cowork for? Based on Anthropic's own usage data, the most common jobs are business process and operations work (33.4% of sessions) and content or copywriting work (16.4%), things like compiling reports, building checklists, reconciling spreadsheets, and drafting business documents.

How do I set it up correctly? Prerequisites, the first-task checklist, and the mistakes worth avoiding are covered in our Claude Cowork setup guide, including the permissions model you should understand before pointing it at anything you can't afford to lose.
